steps.body: Not every object lines up with 0. A pencil from 4 to 10 is 10 − 4 = 6 inches — the same subtraction rule, just with a different starting mark.

widget.prompt: A pencil starts at 4 and ends at 10 on an inch ruler. How long is it?

commonPlacements.feedback: 10 is just the end mark. Subtract the start: 10 − 4 = 6.

widget.alignFeedback: Align zero with the object's starting mark at 4 before counting units.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: Cover only the distance from 4 to 10 with equal units — no gaps, overlaps, or extra units.
widget.unitFeedback: Use one-inch units so the unit count is the length in inches.

explanationVariants: Subtract the start from the end: 8 − 2 = 6.

widget.prompt: A key starts at 2 and ends at 8 on a centimeter ruler. How long is it?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 is just the end mark. Subtract the start: 8 − 2 = 6.

steps.body: A common mix-up is reading just the end mark and forgetting the start. Always check: does the object begin at 0? If not, subtract.

widget.prompt: A spoon starts at 1 and ends at 6 on an inch ruler. How long is it?

commonPlacements.feedback: 6 is just the end mark. Subtract the start: 6 − 1 = 5.

widget.alignFeedback: Align zero with the object's starting mark at 1 before counting units.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: Cover only the distance from 1 to 6 with equal units — no gaps, overlaps, or extra units.
widget.unitFeedback: Use one-inch units so the unit count is the length in inches.

steps.body: The gap between the two marks IS the length — you're counting the inches (or centimeters) the object actually covers, not the position of either end alone.

widget.prompt: A marker starts at 3 and ends at 11 on an inch ruler. How long is it?

commonPlacements.feedback: 11 is just the end mark. Subtract the start: 11 − 3 = 8.

widget.alignFeedback: Align zero with the object's starting mark at 3 before counting units.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: Cover only the distance from 3 to 11 with equal units — no gaps, overlaps, or extra units.
widget.unitFeedback: Use one-inch units so the unit count is the length in inches.

widget.prompt: Which unit is best to measure the length of a crayon?

options.label: inches
options.feedback: Yes — a crayon is small, so inches are the right size unit.

options.label: feet
options.feedback: Feet are for bigger things. A crayon is better measured in inches.

explanationVariants: A playground is large, so feet fit best.

widget.prompt: Which unit is best to measure the length of a playground?

options.label: feet
options.feedback: Yes — a playground is large, so feet are the right size unit.

options.label: inches

explanationVariants: Subtract the start from the end: 12 − 5 = 7.

widget.prompt: A ruler-shaped block starts at 5 and ends at 12 on an inch ruler. How long is it?

commonErrors.feedback: 12 is just the end mark. Subtract the start: 12 − 5 = 7.

hints: Length is end mark minus start mark.

steps.body: Whenever an object doesn't start at 0, subtract to find its true length.
takeaways: Length = end mark − start mark, always.
Reading only the end mark is a common mistake when the start isn't 0.
Match the unit to the size of what you're measuring.

concept.body: When an object doesn't start at 0, subtract the start mark from the end mark to find its length. A pencil from 4 to 10 is 10 − 4 = 6 inches.

explanationVariants: Subtract the start from the end: 6.
